answer: The verifier commits a 64 GB RAM array under a falcon seed and demands nanosecond access proofs before accepting any answer. Each agent walks the array in order while the verifier checks every read against a 120 ns budget, so a pass needs the full array resident. One honest agent spends 0.40 dollars and 3 minutes per proof, while 10 fakes must each hold a separate 64 GB array, paying ten times the memory and time. Timings outside the envelope slash the 500 POA bond and freeze repeat offenders for three epochs, and the pearl latency log with the grove seed is published.
